name: Character modifiers
description: Persistent character variations with concrete implications for play

fields.description: An old injury has left dense scar tissue and a tender weak point; blows or strenuous motion involving it can cause sudden pain and restricted movement.
Their eyes and skin react painfully to strong light; glare impairs perception, and prolonged exposure forces them to seek shade or protection.
A permanent combination of voice, mannerisms, and distinctive features makes them difficult to disguise; witnesses can recognize them after even a brief encounter.
Long exposure has made cold, rain, and rough travel easier to endure, but dulled skin and calloused hands miss faint touch and other fine tactile cues.
The permanent loss of one eye narrows their field of view and depth perception; threats on the blind side and precise distance judgments are harder to notice.
Old smoke, disease, or injury has permanently reduced their breath; sustained exertion, choking air, and holding their breath become serious limitations.
An unmistakable legal, religious, or factional brand marks them; those who understand it may identify them immediately, deny aid, or demand particular conduct.
A persistent ritual bond imposes a prohibition or duty chosen by the GM; approaching a breach produces an obvious warning and invites a fitting complication.
A prosthetic arm or leg restores ordinary function and can brace against some hazards, but fine control or uneven ground is harder and damage requires specialist repair.
Several fingers are permanently missing from one hand; a full grip, fine manipulation, and tools made for two complete hands require adaptation or extra time.
An old injury causes a pronounced limp; sprinting, climbing, and balancing are more difficult, and the uneven gait is easy to track or recognize.
A persistent tremor worsens under stress; steady aim, delicate manipulation, and remaining perfectly still are unreliable even when the character is otherwise capable.
Persistent magical residue clings to them; wards, magical detection, and supernatural predators may notice or react to their presence more readily.
They live with the following persistent affliction: {{ affliction }} The GM determines when and how the condition has concrete consequences in play.
Permanent hearing loss makes quiet speech and the direction of distant sounds difficult to judge, especially amid noise or when danger approaches from the affected side.
A persistent unseen presence disturbs sleep, silence, and attempts at stealth, but its reactions may also warn of nearby supernatural danger.
